summary: Initial POC scoping focused on workload characterization and traffic modeling. Customer wants to validate cost and latency at realistic QPS and concurrency using captured traces. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send proposal and benchmark plan; customer to provide traffic capture and security contacts. Key success criteria: meeting p50/p95 latency targets and cost per 1M tokens within agreed budget; no sensitive data leakage; ability to run in VPC if required.
transcript:
Header: 2025-11-03 15:00 UTC | Duration: 62 mins | Attendees: Priya Menon (Redwood AE), Carlos Ruiz (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Zenith Head of Platform), Tom Becker (Infra Lead), Lucy Park (ML Engineer)

Summary: POC scoping for workload modeling and benchmarks. Focus on QPS, concurrency, token distribution, and timelines.

Topics: success criteria, traffic capture, benchmark config, security/VPC, timeline and next steps.

00:00 Priya Menon: hey everyone thanks for joining, quick intro from our side, i'm priya, lead AE at redwood inference, with carlos our solutions engineer.
00:12 Aisha Khan: thanks, aisha here, head of platform at zenith. we want to scope a POC to validate serving latency and cost for our fraud-detection assistant workflows.
00:25 Carlos Ruiz: great — can you give us a quick sense of current traffic? qps, concurrency, average prompt sizes? even ballpark helps.
00:35 Tom Becker: yeah, right now our sandbox shows spikes up to 150 qps for the assistant during peak hours, sustained 40-60 qps during business hours. concurrency around 30-50 active sessions.
00:52 Lucy Park: average prompt length is about 30-60 input tokens, outputs vary — typical replies 80-150 tokens but we do have longer summarization tasks up to 400 tokens occasionally.
01:10 Priya Menon: ok helpful. when you say 150 qps spikes, is that single short requests or batched flows? are you doing streaming?
01:20 Tom Becker: mostly single-shot requests, we do web-socket streaming for some flows but only about 5-10% of traffic.
01:30 Carlos Ruiz: good — for benchmarking we typically model both steady-state sustained qps and bursty spikes. two things we'll want: a captured traffic replay (anonymized) and a synthetic workload to push to the target qps/concurrency.
01:45 Aisha Khan: re success criteria: we care about latency and cost. target p50 < 120ms and p95 < 450ms for short prompts, and acceptable degradation for longer outputs. is that feasible?
01:58 Carlos Ruiz: depends on model and deployment mode. hosted smaller models can meet p50 ~50-100ms for 0-64 token outputs; p95 in the 200-400ms range at moderate qps. for your 150 qps spikes we may recommend dedicated pools or scaling policy with burst capacity.
02:15 Priya Menon: also worth capturing token distribution shape — median input tokens, 75/95 percentiles, and output token tails. that drives batching and KV cache efficiencies.
02:30 Lucy Park: we can export tokenized traces, we use the same tokenizer as the model (we think). question: how do you handle KV cache and long-context costs?
02:40 Carlos Ruiz: our runtime uses KV cache reuse across streaming sessions where applicable; for long contexts we recommend models with optimized attention or quantized variants to reduce memory and cost. during POC we'll test model variants and a quantized baseline.
02:53 Tom Becker: curious about cost modeling — can you give a sense for cost per 1M tokens at different batch sizes and quant levels?
03:05 Priya Menon: yes we'll include cost estimates per 1M tokens across the configs we test (hosted small model, hosted large, dedicated quantized). we'll tie that back to your traffic to show projected monthly cost.
03:18 Aisha Khan: timeline — we want results within 3 weeks if possible. what's realistic?
03:25 Carlos Ruiz: typical POC timeline: week 0-1: prep and traffic capture; week 2: run benchmarks synthetic + replay; week 3: analysis and recommendations. 3 weeks is tight but doable if traffic capture comes in quickly.
03:40 Priya Menon: ok, sounds aligned. tradeoffs we should explicitly call out: latency vs batching. if we batch aggressively to improve throughput cost per token drops but tail latency can increase — for your realtime assistant we may keep batch sizes conservative and rely on dedicated pools.
03:58 Lucy Park: what about regional routing? we have EU users primarily, need data residency and SOC2.
04:06 Priya Menon: we can run POC in the EU region and provide SOC2 + security FAQ. for private deployments we offer VPC/Private mode but that adds setup time. for POC we'll start hosted in the EU unless you want private immediately.
04:22 Tom Becker: we'll prefer VPC for production but for the POC hosted in VPC sounds heavy — we can do hosted EU first.
04:30 Carlos Ruiz: perfect. for the benchmark configs we'll define target scenarios:
04:35 - Scenario A: Steady 50 qps, concurrency 30, median input 45 tokens, median output 100 tokens.
04:45 - Scenario B: Peak burst 150 qps for 2-5 minutes, concurrency up to 80, mixed prompts (many short 20-40 token requests).
04:55 - Scenario C: Long-tail summarization 10 qps, outputs 200-400 tokens to measure throughput and memory usage.
05:08 Aisha Khan: and what metrics will you report? p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens, GPU utilization, and error rates?
05:16 Carlos Ruiz: yes — plus queueing delays, batching sizes, and a breakdown of how much of cost is model compute vs overhead. we'll also surface recommendations: batching policy, cache TTL, quantization level, and whether dedicated pool is needed.
05:30 Lucy Park: please call out assumptions in the report — e.g., sequence length cap, padding behavior, tokenization differences. we've seen tokenization inflate counts by 10-15% vs naive word counts.
05:42 Priya Menon: noted. small transcription glitch: sometimes customer names or internal tool names get mangled in auto transcripts — we'll confirm exact tokenizer/version.
05:52 Tom Becker: security question: during replay will data be stored on redwood infra? what's retention?
06:00 Priya Menon: for the POC we can accept an anonymized capture. Redwood will store replay data temporarily for the benchmark run and will purge after completion per the DPA; we'll share retention windows. we'll also provide KMS details if you move to private.
06:18 Aisha Khan: ok good. do you have any benchmarking script or agent we should run to capture traces?
06:25 Carlos Ruiz: we can share a small capture tool and format guidelines — but if you already have 48-hour logs that's fine. prefer JSONL with fields: timestamp, request_id, input_text, output_text_len, user_region (anonymized).
06:42 Lucy Park: we can produce that. also want to simulate real concurrency patterns not just qps, so please model session stickiness (same user multiple requests) and KV cache hit rates.
06:55 Carlos Ruiz: absolutely — we will parameterize cache-hit rates. typical cache-hit assumptions we'll test: 0%, 20%, 50% to show cost/latency delta.
07:06 Priya Menon: benchmarks — we'll run both replay and synthetic. replay gives realistic token distribution; synthetic is for controlled stress tests to push peak qps.
07:18 Tom Becker: what about model selection — any recommendations?
07:22 Carlos Ruiz: we'll test two model classes: a fast small/medium model for latency-sensitive short replies and a larger model variant for higher-quality summarization. we'll include a quantized variant for the larger model to show cost savings.
07:36 Aisha Khan: acceptable quality thresholds: for short reply flows we need >=95% acceptable responses per our internal eval (they have a manual eval set). can that be part of the POC?
07:46 Priya Menon: yes we can run automated evals on a holdout prompt set and report quality metrics (BLEU-ish / exact match / human pass rate). tie that to the cost/latency tradeoff.
07:58 Lucy Park: regarding concurrency and batching: what's the expected throughput improvement from batching?
08:03 Carlos Ruiz: depends on model and sequence length. for medium-length tokens (avg 100 tokens) batching can improve GPU throughput 2-3x at the cost of added batching latency; we'll quantify that in the run and recommend a batching window that balances tail latency.
08:22 Tom Becker: note — our SLO is stricter for fraud flows (must be sub-200ms p50). those will be routed to a higher-priority pool in production. can the POC test priority routing?
08:36 Carlos Ruiz: yes we can simulate multi-tier routing: high-priority low-latency pool for fraud at smaller batch sizes and a cost-optimized pool for non-critical tasks. we'll simulate that in the benchmark.
08:49 Aisha Khan: great. cost cap: we'd like to evaluate options where monthly inference cost stays under $X (redacted). can you produce cost projections?
08:58 Priya Menon: yes cost projections per model/config will be in the final deck. we'll show best/worst case based on your 48-hour trace scaled to monthly.
09:07 Lucy Park: any constraints around SAML/SSO for console access during POC?
09:12 Priya Menon: we can provide invite-only access; full SSO set up typically takes longer but we can do scoped service accounts for the POC.
09:22 Tom Becker: ok next steps recap?
09:25 Priya Menon: recap: 1) Red wood to send POC proposal + pricing and benchmark plan (pri-ya), 2) Zenith to provide 48-hour anonymized traffic capture and eval prompts (lucy and aisha), 3) redwood to run benchmarks week of 11/17, 4) sync to review results week of 11/24.
09:45 Aisha Khan: sounds good. one more quick question — do you support on-prem private deployment for production?
09:51 Carlos Ruiz: yes — private/VPC is an option for production. that'll be a separate engagement with extra setup time and entitlements. we can include a high-level estimate in the proposal.
10:02 Tom Becker: thanks everyone. we'll aim to get the capture to you by 11/10.
10:06 Priya Menon: thanks — i'll follow up with docs (security FAQ, SOC2, architecture) and the POC deck. thanks all.
